title: MATH GAOKAO - 8
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Find the difference of two finite sets given in roster notation.
questions.question: Let \(A=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(B=\{2,3,4\}\). What is \(A\setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: The difference \(A\setminus B\) consists of all elements that belong to \(A\) but not to \(B\). In \(A=\{1,2,3\}\), the elements \(2\) and \(3\) also belong to \(B\), so they are removed. The only remaining element is \(1\). Therefore \(A\setminus B=\{1\}\).
questions.hint: Remove from \(A\) every element that also appears in \(B\).

questions.concept: Difference of Sets in Roster Notation
questions.learningObjective: Determine the difference of two finite sets with a common element.
questions.question: Let \(A=\{a,b,c\}\) and \(B=\{b,d\}\). What is \(A\setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: The set \(A\setminus B\) contains the elements of \(A\) that are not in \(B\). Since \(b\in B\), it is removed from \(A\). The elements \(a\) and \(c\) are not in \(B\), so they remain. Therefore \(A\setminus B=\{a,c\}\).
questions.hint: List the elements of \(A\), then delete any element that belongs to \(B\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the difference of two overlapping real intervals.
questions.question: Let \(A=[1,4)\) and \(B=[2,5)\). What is \(A\setminus B\)?
questions.explanation:
The interval \(A=[1,4)\) contains all real numbers from \(1\) up to but not including \(4\). The interval \(B=[2,5)\) contains all real numbers from \(2\) up to but not including \(5\). Removing the elements of \(B\) from \(A\) leaves the numbers from \(1\) up to but not including \(2\). Since \(2\in B\), it is excluded. Therefore
\[
A\setminus B=[1,2).
\]
questions.hint: Find the part of \(A\) that lies outside \(B\), paying attention to whether endpoints belong to \(B\).

questions.concept: Difference of Sets Given in Set-Builder Notation
questions.learningObjective: Convert two sets from set-builder notation to roster form and find their difference.
questions.question: Let \(A=\{x\in\mathbb Z\mid -1\le x\le 3\}\) and \(B=\{x\in\mathbb N^+\mid x<4\}\). What is \(A\setminus B\) in roster form?
questions.explanation:
The set \(A\) consists of the integers from \(-1\) to \(3\), so \(A=\{-1,0,1,2,3\}\). The set \(B\) consists of positive integers less than \(4\), so \(B=\{1,2,3\}\). Removing the elements of \(B\) from \(A\) leaves \(-1\) and \(0\). Therefore
\[
A\setminus B=\{-1,0\}.
\]
questions.hint: Write both sets in roster form first, then remove the elements of \(B\) from \(A\).

questions.learningObjective: Use the cardinality of an intersection to find the number of elements in a set difference.
questions.question: Let \(A\) and \(B\) be finite sets with \(|A|=10\), \(|B|=6\), and \(|A\cap B|=4\). How many elements are in \(A\setminus B\)?
questions.explanation:
The elements of \(A\setminus B\) are exactly the elements of \(A\) that are not in \(A\cap B\). Therefore
\[
|A\setminus B|=|A|-|A\cap B|=10-4=6.
\]
Hence \(A\setminus B\) has \(6\) elements.
questions.hint: Subtract the number of elements shared by \(A\) and \(B\) from the total number of elements in \(A\).

questions.concept: Difference of a Set with Itself
questions.learningObjective: Apply the property that the difference of a set with itself is empty.
questions.question: For any set \(A\), what is \(A\setminus A\)?
questions.explanation:
The set \(A\setminus A\) consists of elements that belong to \(A\) but not to \(A\). No element can satisfy both conditions at the same time. Therefore
\[
A\setminus A=\varnothing.
\]
questions.hint: Ask whether any element can be in \(A\) and simultaneously not in \(A\).

questions.learningObjective: Find the complement of a finite set relative to a universal set using set difference.
questions.question: Let \(U=\{1,2,3,4,5\}\) and \(A=\{1,2,3\}\). What is \(U\setminus A\)?
questions.explanation:
The difference \(U\setminus A\) contains the elements of \(U\) that are not in \(A\). Removing \(1,2,3\) from \(U=\{1,2,3,4,5\}\) leaves \(4\) and \(5\). Therefore
\[
U\setminus A=\{4,5\}.
\]
questions.hint: Start with all elements of \(U\) and delete every element that belongs to \(A\).

questions.concept: Parameter from a Set Difference Condition
questions.learningObjective: Determine an unknown element that makes a set difference equal to a given set.
questions.question: Let \(A=\{1,2,a\}\) and \(B=\{2,3\}\). If \(A\setminus B=\{1,4\}\), what is the value of \(a\)?
questions.explanation:
The set \(A\setminus B\) contains the elements of \(A\) that are not in \(B\). Since \(2\in B\), it is removed. The element \(1\) is already in \(A\setminus B\). To obtain \(A\setminus B=\{1,4\}\), the element \(a\) must be \(4\). If \(a=3\), then \(3\in B\), so \(3\) would be removed and \(A\setminus B\) would not contain \(4\). Therefore
\[
a=4.
\]
questions.hint: Identify which elements of \(A\) are removed by \(B\), then match the remaining elements with the given difference.

questions.concept: Difference of Unbounded and Bounded Intervals
questions.learningObjective: Determine the simplified interval form of the difference of two real intervals.
questions.question: Let \(A=(-\infty,4)\) and \(B=(-1,2]\). What is \(A\setminus B\)?
questions.explanation:
The interval \(A=(-\infty,4)\) contains all real numbers less than \(4\). The interval \(B=(-1,2]\) contains all real numbers greater than \(-1\) and at most \(2\). Removing \(B\) from \(A\) leaves the numbers less than or equal to \(-1\), together with the numbers greater than \(2\) and less than \(4\). Since \(-1\notin B\), it remains, while \(2\in B\), so it is removed. Therefore
\[
A\setminus B=(-\infty,-1]\cup(2,4).
\]
questions.hint: Remove the overlapping part \((-1,2]\) from \(A\), and check carefully whether \(-1\) and \(2\) remain.

questions.concept: Difference of Integer Sets Defined by Inequalities
questions.learningObjective: Convert two sets defined by inequalities over the integers into roster form and find their difference.
questions.question: Let \(A=\{x\in\mathbb Z\mid x^2<16\}\) and \(B=\{x\in\mathbb Z\mid |x|\le 2\}\). What is \(A\setminus B\) in roster form?
questions.explanation:
The inequality \(x^2<16\) is equivalent to \(-4<x<4\), so
\[
A=\{-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3\}.
\]
The inequality \(|x|\le 2\) gives
\[
B=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}.
\]
Removing the elements of \(B\) from \(A\) leaves \(-3\) and \(3\). Therefore
\[
A\setminus B=\{-3,3\}.
\]
questions.hint: Write both sets in roster form first, then remove from \(A\) every element that belongs to \(B\).
